```{r}
metadata <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "01_metadata.csv"))
species  <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "02_microbiome_counts.csv"))    
taxonomy <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "03_microbiome_taxonomy.csv"))
genes    <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "04_rnaseq_counts.csv.gz")) 
genes_2_annot <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "05_gene_annotation.csv"))
```

## Do the three methods differ in community composition?

Each point is a sample, colored by its contraceptive arm (injectable, pill, or
ring). Samples closer together have more similar species compositions under
the chosen distance.

### No they don't differ ni the community composition

```{r}
# Build the phyloseq object from the data frames loaded above.
sample_ids <- names(species)[-1]
feature_ids <- as.character(species[[1]])

if (!setequal(metadata$sample_id, sample_ids)) {
  stop("The species-table sample columns do not match metadata$sample_id.")
}
if (!setequal(feature_ids, taxonomy$taxon)) {
  stop("The species-table features do not match taxonomy$taxon.")
}

count_matrix <- as.matrix(species[, -1])
storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"
rownames(count_matrix) <- feature_ids

taxonomy_matrix <- as.matrix(taxonomy[
  match(feature_ids, taxonomy$taxon),
  setdiff(names(taxonomy), "taxon"),
  drop = FALSE
])
storage.mode(taxonomy_matrix) <- "character"
rownames(taxonomy_matrix) <- feature_ids

metadata_for_ps <- as.data.frame(metadata)
metadata_for_ps <- metadata_for_ps[
  match(sample_ids, metadata_for_ps$sample_id),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
rownames(metadata_for_ps) <- metadata_for_ps$sample_id

arm_levels <- c("injectable", "pill", "ring")
metadata_for_ps$arm <- factor(metadata_for_ps$arm, levels = arm_levels)

ps_species <- phyloseq::phyloseq(
  phyloseq::otu_table(count_matrix, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
  phyloseq::sample_data(metadata_for_ps),
  phyloseq::tax_table(taxonomy_matrix)
)

bray_plot <- ps_species |>
  tax_transform("identity", rank = "species") |>
  dist_calc("bray") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA") |>
  ord_plot(colour = "arm") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Bray-Curtis")

jaccard_plot <- ps_species |>
  tax_transform("binary", rank = "species") |>
  dist_calc("jaccard") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA") |>
  ord_plot(colour = "arm") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Jaccard")

aitchison_plot <- ps_species |>
  tax_transform("identity", rank = "species") |>
  dist_calc("aitchison") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA") |>
  ord_plot(colour = "arm") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Aitchison")

community_plot <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  bray_plot,
  jaccard_plot,
  aitchison_plot,
  ncol = 3,
  guides = "collect"
) &
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

community_plot

dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

ggplot2::ggsave(

)
```

PERMANOVA tests whether community composition differs among arms. R² is the
proportion of variation associated with arm; F is the test statistic; and the
p-value measures evidence against no arm-associated difference. Interpret
these alongside the plots and check group dispersion, since unequal within-arm
spread can affect PERMANOVA.

```{r}
run_arm_permanova <- function(distance_name, transform_name) {
  result <- ps_species |>
    tax_transform(transform_name, rank = "species") |>
    dist_calc(distance_name) |>
    dist_permanova(variables = "arm", n_perms = 999, seed = 1) |>
    perm_get() |>
    as.data.frame()

  tibble::tibble(
    distance = distance_name,
    R2 = result["arm", "R2"],
    F = result["arm", "F"],
    p_value = result["arm", "Pr(>F)"]
  )
}

permanova_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_arm_permanova("bray", "identity"),
  run_arm_permanova("jaccard", "binary"),
  run_arm_permanova("aitchison", "identity")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    distance = factor(
      distance,
      levels = c("bray", "jaccard", "aitchison"),
      labels = c("Bray-Curtis", "Jaccard", "Aitchison")
    )
  )

permanova_table_data <- permanova_results |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_value = dplyr::if_else(
      p_value < 0.001,
      "<0.001",
      sprintf("%.3f", p_value)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Test = distance,
    `R-squared (R²)` = R2,
    `F statistic` = F,
    `P-value` = p_value
  )

permanova_gt <- gt::gt(permanova_table_data) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title = gt::md("**PERMANOVA: Community composition by contraceptive arm**"),
    subtitle = "Tests compare injectable, pill, and ring groups (999 permutations)"
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `R-squared (R²)`, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `F statistic`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::cols_label(Test = "Distance metric") |>
  gt::cols_align(align = "center", columns = -Test) |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.width = gt::pct(100),
    table.font.size = gt::px(14),
    heading.title.font.size = gt::px(16),
    data_row.padding = gt::px(6),
    row.striping.include_table_body = TRUE
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = gt::md(
      "R² is the proportion of community variation associated with contraceptive arm. P-values below 0.001 are shown as <0.001."
    )
  )

permanova_gt

table_dir <- here::here("group_project", "table")
dir.create(table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

gt::gtsave(
  permanova_gt,
  filename = file.path(table_dir, "community_permanova_group_2.html")
)
```

### Community analysis choices

- Distance: Bray-Curtis, Jaccard, and Aitchison; alternative: compare only one distance.
- Transform: identity for Bray-Curtis and Aitchison, binary for Jaccard; alternative: use one transform for all.
- Ordination: PCoA; alternative: NMDS.
- Test: PERMANOVA with 999 permutations and seed 1; alternative: parametric tests on individual taxa.
- Grouping: injectable, pill, and ring arms; alternative: test another metadata variable.
- Samples dropped: none; alternative: apply a prespecified sequencing-depth threshold.


### Is bacterial vaginosis more common in one arm? 

#### Approach

I will compare the percentage of participants with **positive BV** across the
injectable, pill, and ring arms. For this comparison, negative and intermediate
results are grouped as **not positive**; I will also show all three original
BV categories in a separate table so the intermediate results remain visible.
The main test is a Pearson chi-square test on the 2-by-3 table (positive versus
not positive by arm). The code checks the expected cell counts and switches to
Fisher's exact test if any expected count is below 5. This tests an association,
not whether the contraceptive method caused BV. P-values are reported to three
decimal places.

```{r}
bv_arm_levels <- c("injectable", "pill", "ring")
bv_categories <- c("negative", "intermediate", "positive")

if (!all(c("arm", "bv") %in% names(metadata))) {
  stop("metadata must contain arm and bv columns.")
}
if (anyNA(metadata$arm) || anyNA(metadata$bv)) {
  stop("Missing arm or BV values must be resolved before this comparison.")
}
if (!all(metadata$arm %in% bv_arm_levels)) {
  stop("Unexpected arm values found in metadata.")
}
if (!all(metadata$bv %in% bv_categories)) {
  stop("Unexpected BV categories found; check metadata$bv.")
}

bv_data <- metadata %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    arm = factor(arm, levels = bv_arm_levels),
    bv = factor(bv, levels = bv_categories),
    bv_status = factor(
      ifelse(bv == "positive", "Positive", "Not positive"),
      levels = c("Not positive", "Positive")
    )
  )

# Descriptive table: retain negative, intermediate, and positive BV categories.
bv_categories_table <- gtsummary::tbl_cross(
  data = bv_data,
  row = bv,
  col = arm,
  percent = "column",
  margin = "column",
  digits = 1,
  label = list(bv ~ "BV category", arm ~ "Contraceptive arm")
) %>%
  gtsummary::modify_caption(
    "**BV categories by contraceptive arm**"
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::bold_labels()

# Primary test: compare positive BV with negative/intermediate across arms.
bv_status_counts <- table(bv_data$bv_status, bv_data$arm)
bv_chisq <- stats::chisq.test(bv_status_counts, correct = FALSE)

# Fisher's exact test is safer if the chi-square expected counts are too small.
if (any(bv_chisq$expected < 5)) {
  bv_test <- "fisher.test"
  bv_test_name <- "Fisher's exact test"
} else {
  bv_test <- "chisq.test"
  bv_test_name <- "Pearson chi-square test"
}

bv_prevalence_table <- gtsummary::tbl_cross(
  data = bv_data,
  row = bv_status,
  col = arm,
  percent = "column",
  margin = "column",
  digits = 1,
  label = list(bv_status ~ "BV status", arm ~ "Contraceptive arm")
) %>%
  gtsummary::add_p(
    test = bv_test,
    pvalue_fun = gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 3)
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::modify_caption(
    "**Positive BV prevalence by contraceptive arm**"
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::modify_footnote(
    gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~
      paste0(
        "Values are participant counts and percentages within arm. ",
        bv_test_name,
        " compares positive with not-positive BV; p-values are shown to 3 decimal places."
      )
  ) %>%
  gtsummary::bold_labels()

bv_categories_table
bv_prevalence_table

bv_table_dir <- here::here("group_project", "tables")
dir.create(bv_table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

gt::gtsave(
  gtsummary::as_gt(bv_categories_table),
  filename = file.path(bv_table_dir, "bv_categories_by_arm_group_2.html")
)
gt::gtsave(
  gtsummary::as_gt(bv_prevalence_table),
  filename = file.path(bv_table_dir, "bv_prevalence_by_arm_group_2.html")
)
```


### The ring is delivered locally and the other two are systemic. Does the ring differ from the other two in host gene expression? start by ordinating the genes.

#### Approach

I will combine the pill and injectable arms into one **systemic** group and
compare it with the **ring** group. First, I will make a PCA plot from
variance-stabilized gene counts to see whether samples cluster by delivery
group or RNA-seq batch. This is an exploratory overview, not a significance
test. Then I will use DESeq2 on the original raw gene counts (not CPM or logged
counts), adjusting for `rnaseq_batch`. Before testing, the code checks sample
IDs and aligns the count columns to the metadata.

I will filter out genes with fewer than 10 reads in at least 10 samples, then
use Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values (`padj`) to account for testing many
genes. Positive log2 fold changes mean higher expression in the ring group.
This tests an association in this dataset; it does not show that local delivery
caused any expression difference.

The code saves the plots as PNG and PDF, and saves the full results, test
summary, and top 20 genes as CSV files in `group_project/`.

```{r}
feature_id_col <- names(genes)[1]
sample_ids <- names(genes)[-1]

if (!all(c("sample_id", "arm", "rnaseq_batch") %in% names(metadata))) {
  stop("metadata must contain sample_id, arm, and rnaseq_batch.")
}
if (anyNA(metadata$sample_id) || anyDuplicated(metadata$sample_id)) {
  stop("metadata sample IDs are missing or duplicated.")
}
if (!setequal(sample_ids, metadata$sample_id)) {
  stop("RNA-seq sample columns do not match metadata$sample_id.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(sample_ids)) {
  stop("The RNA-seq table contains duplicated sample columns.")
}
if (anyNA(genes[[feature_id_col]]) || anyDuplicated(genes[[feature_id_col]])) {
  stop("RNA-seq feature IDs are missing or duplicated.")
}
if (!all(metadata$arm %in% c("ring", "pill", "injectable"))) {
  stop("Unexpected or missing contraceptive arm values in metadata.")
}
if (anyNA(metadata$rnaseq_batch)) {
  stop("Some samples are missing their RNA-seq batch assignment.")
}

# Keep the raw counts and align their columns to the metadata rows.
gene_counts <- as.matrix(genes[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE])
storage.mode(gene_counts) <- "numeric"
rownames(gene_counts) <- as.character(genes[[feature_id_col]])
gene_counts <- gene_counts[, metadata$sample_id, drop = FALSE]

if (any(!is.finite(gene_counts)) || any(gene_counts < 0)) {
  stop("RNA-seq counts contain missing, non-finite, or negative values.")
}
if (any(abs(gene_counts - round(gene_counts)) > 1e-8)) {
  stop("DESeq2 requires raw integer counts; non-integer values were found.")
}
storage.mode(gene_counts) <- "integer"

gene_coldata <- metadata %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_id, arm, rnaseq_batch) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    delivery_group = factor(
      ifelse(arm == "ring", "ring", "systemic"),
      levels = c("systemic", "ring")
    ),
    rnaseq_batch = factor(rnaseq_batch)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
rownames(gene_coldata) <- gene_coldata$sample_id

# Check whether batch and delivery group can be estimated separately.
design_matrix <- stats::model.matrix(
  ~ rnaseq_batch + delivery_group,
  data = gene_coldata
)
if (qr(design_matrix)$rank < ncol(design_matrix)) {
  stop("RNA-seq batch is confounded with delivery group; cannot fit both terms.")
}

# Prefilter genes with fewer than 10 reads in at least 10 samples.
keep_gene <- rowSums(gene_counts >= 10) >= 10
gene_counts_filtered <- gene_counts[keep_gene, , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(gene_counts_filtered) == 0) {
  stop("No genes passed the expression filter.")
}

# Explore overall sample patterns using a variance-stabilizing transformation.
dds_for_pca <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = gene_counts_filtered,
  colData = gene_coldata,
  design = ~ rnaseq_batch + delivery_group
)
vsd <- DESeq2::vst(dds_for_pca, blind = TRUE)
pca_data <- DESeq2::plotPCA(
  vsd,
  intgroup = c("delivery_group", "rnaseq_batch"),
  returnData = TRUE
)
pca_percent <- round(100 * attr(pca_data, "percentVar"))

gene_pca_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  pca_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = PC1,
    y = PC2,
    color = delivery_group,
    shape = rnaseq_batch
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "PCA of host gene expression",
    subtitle = "Ring versus systemic contraceptive arms",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", pca_percent[1], "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", pca_percent[2], "%)"),
    color = "Delivery group",
    shape = "RNA-seq batch"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

gene_pca_plot

gene_plot_dir <- here::here("group_project", "plots")
dir.create(gene_plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(
  file.path(gene_plot_dir, "host_gene_pca_ring_vs_systemic_group_2.png"),
  plot = gene_pca_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
ggplot2::ggsave(
  file.path(gene_plot_dir, "host_gene_pca_ring_vs_systemic_group_2.pdf"),
  plot = gene_pca_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6
)

dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = gene_counts_filtered,
  colData = gene_coldata,
  design = ~ rnaseq_batch + delivery_group
)
dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds)

# Positive log2 fold changes mean higher expression in ring than systemic.
gene_results <- DESeq2::results(
  dds,
  contrast = c("delivery_group", "ring", "systemic"),
  alpha = 0.05
)

gene_results_table <- as.data.frame(gene_results) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(feature_id_col) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    genes_2_annot,
    by = stats::setNames("ensembl_gene_id", feature_id_col)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(padj)

gene_test_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  samples_ring = sum(gene_coldata$delivery_group == "ring"),
  samples_systemic = sum(gene_coldata$delivery_group == "systemic"),
  genes_tested = nrow(gene_results_table),
  genes_with_adjusted_p_below_0_05 = sum(gene_results_table$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
)

knitr::kable(gene_test_summary, caption = "DESeq2 test summary")
knitr::kable(
  gene_results_table %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(feature_id_col), symbol, gene_name,
      baseMean, log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj
    ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Top 20 genes by adjusted p-value"
)

gene_results_dir <- here::here("group_project")
readr::write_csv(
  gene_results_table,
  file.path(gene_results_dir, "genes_ring_vs_systemic_group_2.csv")
)

head(gene_results_table)

readr::write_csv(
  gene_test_summary,
  file.path(gene_results_dir, "genes_ring_vs_systemic_summary_group_2.csv")
)
readr::write_csv(
  gene_results_table %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(feature_id_col), symbol, gene_name,
      baseMean, log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj
    ),
  file.path(gene_results_dir, "genes_ring_vs_systemic_top20_group_2.csv")
)
```

### What else could explain the gene patterns?

PC1 explains about a third of the variation, but neither delivery group nor
batch lines up with it. These plots colour the same PCA by BV status, by the
three arms, and by pH, to see what PC1 is picking up. The PERMANOVA then asks
one overall question: do ring and systemic samples differ across all genes
together, after accounting for batch? The dispersion test checks that any
difference is not just one group being more spread out.

```{r}
# Reuse the variance-stabilized counts (vsd) from the PCA above.
# pca_data already carries sample_id and arm, so only add bv and ph.
pca_extra <- pca_data %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    metadata %>% dplyr::select(sample_id, bv, ph),
    by = "sample_id"
  )

pca_labs <- ggplot2::labs(
  x = paste0("PC1 (", pca_percent[1], "%)"),
  y = paste0("PC2 (", pca_percent[2], "%)")
)

ggplot2::ggplot(pca_extra, ggplot2::aes(PC1, PC2, color = bv)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Host gene PCA coloured by BV status", color = "BV") +
  pca_labs + ggplot2::theme_minimal()

ggplot2::ggplot(pca_extra, ggplot2::aes(PC1, PC2, color = arm)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Host gene PCA coloured by arm", color = "Arm") +
  pca_labs + ggplot2::theme_minimal()

ggplot2::ggplot(pca_extra, ggplot2::aes(PC1, PC2, color = ph)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_c() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Host gene PCA coloured by vaginal pH", color = "pH") +
  pca_labs + ggplot2::theme_minimal()

# PERMANOVA: Euclidean distance on vst values (the same space as the PCA).
vst_matrix <- t(SummarizedExperiment::assay(vsd))
vst_dist <- stats::dist(vst_matrix)
perm_data <- gene_coldata[rownames(vst_matrix), , drop = FALSE]

set.seed(1)
gene_permanova <- vegan::adonis2(
  vst_dist ~ rnaseq_batch + delivery_group,
  data = perm_data,
  permutations = 999,
  by = "terms"
)
gene_permanova

# Is the spread of samples around each group's centre similar?
gene_dispersion <- vegan::betadisper(vst_dist, perm_data$delivery_group)
set.seed(1)
vegan::permutest(gene_dispersion, permutations = 999)
```

### Visualize the differential-expression results

The volcano plot shows the estimated change and adjusted p-value for every
tested gene. The boxplots show variance-stabilized expression for up to six
top-ranked genes, and the heatmap shows the top 20 genes across samples. These
are visual summaries; the DESeq2 adjusted p-values remain the basis for
statistical evidence.

```{r}
volcano_data <- gene_results_table %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), is.finite(log2FoldChange)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    neg_log10_padj = -log10(pmax(padj, .Machine$double.xmin)),
    result = dplyr::if_else(
      padj < 0.05,
      ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0, "Higher in ring", "Higher in systemic"),
      "Not significant"
    )
  )

volcano_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  volcano_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = neg_log10_padj, color = result)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.65, size = 1.4) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(0.05),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey35"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "grey35"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Higher in ring" = "#B2182B",
      "Higher in systemic" = "#2166AC",
      "Not significant" = "grey70"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Differential host gene expression",
    subtitle = "Ring versus systemic arms; DESeq2 adjusted p-values",
    x = "Log2 fold change (ring / systemic)",
    y = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value")),
    color = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

volcano_plot

ranked_genes <- gene_results_table %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(padj)
if (nrow(ranked_genes) == 0) {
  stop("No genes have an adjusted p-value available for plotting.")
}

boxplot_gene_ids <- ranked_genes %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 6) %>%
  dplyr::pull(dplyr::all_of(feature_id_col))

vst_matrix <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(vsd)
boxplot_data <- as.data.frame(vst_matrix[boxplot_gene_ids, , drop = FALSE]) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("feature_id") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -feature_id,
    names_to = "sample_id",
    values_to = "vst_expression"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    gene_coldata %>%
      dplyr::select(sample_id, delivery_group, rnaseq_batch),
    by = "sample_id"
  )

boxplot_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  boxplot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = delivery_group, y = vst_expression, fill = delivery_group)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ feature_id, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Expression of the six top-ranked genes",
    x = "Delivery group",
    y = "Variance-stabilized expression",
    fill = "Delivery group"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")

boxplot_plot

heatmap_gene_ids <- ranked_genes %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 20) %>%
  dplyr::pull(dplyr::all_of(feature_id_col))
heatmap_matrix <- vst_matrix[heatmap_gene_ids, , drop = FALSE]
heatmap_z <- t(scale(t(heatmap_matrix)))
heatmap_z[!is.finite(heatmap_z)] <- 0

heatmap_data <- as.data.frame(heatmap_z) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("feature_id") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -feature_id,
    names_to = "sample_id",
    values_to = "row_z_score"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    gene_coldata %>%
      dplyr::select(sample_id, delivery_group, rnaseq_batch),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    feature_id = factor(feature_id, levels = rev(heatmap_gene_ids)),
    sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = gene_coldata$sample_id)
  )

heatmap_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  heatmap_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = sample_id, y = feature_id, fill = row_z_score)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    ~ delivery_group,
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free_x",
    switch = "x"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#B2182B",
    name = "Gene\nz-score"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Top 20 genes across samples",
    subtitle = "Genes ranked by adjusted p-value; samples grouped by delivery arm",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Gene ID"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.placement = "outside"
  )

volcano_plot
boxplot_plot
heatmap_plot

)
```

## Choices made

- Community distances: Bray-Curtis, Jaccard, and Aitchison; alternative: use only one distance.
- Community transform: identity for Bray-Curtis and Aitchison, binary for Jaccard; alternative: use one transform for all.
- Community ordination: PCoA; alternative: NMDS.
- Community test: PERMANOVA with 999 permutations and seed 1; alternative: parametric tests on individual taxa.
- Community grouping: injectable, pill, and ring; alternative: test another metadata variable.
- Gene-expression ordination: PCA of variance-stabilized counts, colored by delivery group and shaped by RNA-seq batch; alternative: UMAP or PCoA.
- Gene-expression overall test: PERMANOVA (999 permutations, seed 1) on Euclidean distance of variance-stabilized counts, batch entered first; alternative: Bray-Curtis or Aitchison distance.
- Gene-expression spread check: betadisper dispersion test; alternative: skip it and rely on PERMANOVA alone.
- Gene-expression PCA extras: coloured by BV, arm and pH; alternative: add BV as a term in the DESeq2 model.
- Gene-expression test: DESeq2 on raw counts, ring versus pill plus injectable; alternative: compare the three arms separately.
- Gene-expression model: adjust for RNA-seq batch; alternative: omit batch if it was not part of the design.
- Gene filter: at least 10 reads in at least 10 samples; alternative: use a stricter or looser prespecified filter.
- Gene-expression plots: volcano plot, boxplots for the six top-ranked genes, and a row-scaled heatmap for the top 20; alternative: choose genes using a fixed fold-change threshold.
- BV comparison: Pearson chi-square for positive versus not-positive BV when expected counts are all at least 5, otherwise Fisher's exact test; alternative: test the full three-category distribution.
- Samples dropped: none; alternative: exclude samples only for a documented QC reason.
